look: Baghdad: flat-roofed buff brick and concrete buildings, tangled overhead power cables, satellite dishes, white-and-orange taxis, date palms along the Tigris, hazy golden light, mix of old brick lanes and modern glass towers.

Karrada, Baghdad: busy commercial street, shop signs in Arabic stacked above arcades, jewellery and clothes shops, restaurants with grills smoking at the entrance, cafes with tea glasses, dense traffic of taxis and minibuses, trees along the pavement, riverside Abu Nuwas direction nearby.

Al-Mutanabbi Street, Baghdad: pedestrian street lined with open-front bookshops, tables and carts of stacked books, old brick facades with wooden balconies, Al-Shabandar Cafe with framed old photos on the walls, crowds browsing on Friday, a statue of the poet Al-Mutanabbi near the river end.

Tahrir Square, Baghdad: large open traffic square, the Freedom Monument (Nasb al-Hurriyah, a long bronze-and-stone relief by Jawad Saleem) on a raised plinth on one side, busy roundabout, Turkish Restaurant building (Jumhuriya bridge side) visible, flags, taxis and pedestrians.

Abu Nuwas Street, Baghdad: tree-lined Tigris corniche, riverside restaurants, grilled masgouf fish cooking on wooden stakes around fire, benches facing the river, families walking at dusk, boats on the water.
The Tigris: wide brown-green river, concrete and reed banks, date palms, small wooden boats, bridges (Jumhuriya, Sinak, Shuhada) in the distance, golden sunset reflection.
Baghdad shanashil houses: old brick houses with projecting enclosed wooden bay windows (shanashil) carved with lattice, narrow shaded alleys, ornate wooden doors with brass studs.
Al-Kadhimiya shrine, Baghdad: two golden domes and four golden minarets over a marble and mirrored-tile courtyard, turquoise and gold tilework, crowds of pilgrims, bustling market streets around it.

Al-Adhamiya, Baghdad: old neighbourhood on the east Tigris bank, Abu Hanifa Mosque with a large dome and slender minaret, traditional cafes, narrow lanes, Imam al-Adham street with sweet and kebab shops.
Al-Mansour, Baghdad: upscale district, wide tree-lined avenues, modern malls, cafes and boutiques, 14 Ramadan street, glass-front restaurants, well-kept villas.
Al-Zawraa Park, Baghdad: large green park with long paths, lakes, a small Ferris wheel and amusement rides, flower beds, families picnicking, tall eucalyptus and palm trees.
Samarra: the Great Mosque's Malwiya spiral minaret of baked brick rising from a vast empty courtyard of earthen walls, flat desert plain, golden-domed al-Askari shrine in the town.

Najaf: the golden dome and minarets of the Imam Ali shrine, white marble courtyards and mirrored arcades, vast Wadi al-Salam cemetery of white tombs stretching to the horizon, pilgrims in black and white.
Karbala: the twin gold-domed shrines of Imam Hussein and Abbas facing each other along a pedestrian walkway, green and red flags, mirror-work ceilings, crowds of pilgrims, Bayn al-Haramayn avenue.

Basra: Shatt al-Arab river with date palm groves on both banks, old canals ('Venice of the East') with wooden boats, Corniche promenade, humid hot air, port cranes and oil flares in the distance, Ottoman-style brick houses with wooden balconies.
Shatt al-Arab, Basra: wide river where the Tigris and Euphrates meet, palm groves on the banks, tankers and small boats, corniche with walkways and statues, orange sunset haze.

Erbil: the ancient Citadel on its oval hill (honey-coloured walls and gate), Shar Park and the circular bazaar square below it with Mudhafaria minaret nearby, modern towers and malls, Kurdish baggy trousers (sharwal) and sashes, mountains on the horizon.
Sulaymaniyah: city under mountain ridges, Azadi Park, lively tea houses, Kurdish cultural centre atmosphere, Salim Street cafes, snow on the peaks in winter.
Duhok: green mountain valley, Duhok dam lake, Zawa tourist area, mountain villages, cool air, pine and oak slopes, Kurdish folk dress.

Mosul: the Tigris crossing the city, Al-Hadba leaning minaret next to Al-Nuri Mosque ruins being rebuilt, old city lanes of pale limestone (Mosul stone) with arched doorways, new bridges, rebuilt markets.
Kirkuk: ancient citadel mound in the centre, old bazaar, oil flames on the plain around, mixed Arab, Kurdish and Turkmen culture, Turkmen clothing.

Babylon: reconstructed mud-brick ruins of the Ishtar Gate with blue glazed bricks and golden bulls and dragons, massive brick walls, Saddam-era palace on the hill, palm trees, dry heat, Hillah town and the Euphrates nearby.
Ziggurat of Ur, Dhi Qar: a massive stepped mud-brick temple platform with three long staircases rising from a flat desert plain, warm sand colours, wide sky.

Southern Iraqi marshes (Ahwar): tall reed beds, narrow channels, traditional tarada wooden canoes poled by men, mudhif houses built from woven reeds, water buffalo wading, flocks of birds, soft misty light.
Nasiriyah: Euphrates river crossings, old bridges, marsh culture nearby, ziggurat of Ur outside the city, palm groves and brick houses.
Dhi Qar province: flat southern plain, marsh channels, ziggurat of Ur, villages of mud-brick and reed, buffalo herds.
Amarah: Tigris river with a riverside corniche, Maysan marshes nearby, reed boats, palm trees, simple brick buildings.
Kut: Tigris riverside with the Kut barrage, corniche, palms, brick buildings and local markets.
Diwaniyah: Euphrates canals, flat farmland, rice and wheat fields, palm groves, brick houses.
Samawah: Euphrates banks, desert edge, palm groves, the quiet southern desert highway.
Ramadi: Euphrates river, palm groves, rebuilt streets and bridges, western desert plain.
Fallujah: Euphrates river bridges, mosques with tall minarets, palm groves, brick and concrete houses on a flat plain.
Tikrit: Tigris riverbank, palm trees, the large presidential-palace compound by the river, brick houses and mosques.
Duhok dam: large turquoise reservoir between steep green mountains, a road along the shore, restaurants on the water.
Halabja: green plain at the foot of the Hawraman mountains, cool air, Kurdish village houses, orchards.
Rawanduz and Gali Ali Beg: deep rocky gorge with a thundering waterfall, steep mountain road, cliffs with clouds, fresh green slopes.
Iraqi Kurdistan: green rolling mountains, snow-capped peaks in winter, small stone and concrete villages, orchards and streams, Kurdish traditional clothing (sharwal, sashes, colourful dresses).
Iraqi desert: flat sandy and stony plain, power pylons along a long straight highway, dust haze, scattered scrub, low sun with long shadows.
Baghdad's Tigris bridges (Jumhuriya, Shuhada, Sinak): steel arch or girder bridges, heavy traffic, river below with boats, the skyline of old and new buildings.
Sheikh Abdul Qadir Gaylani mosque, Baghdad: large green-and-white-tiled dome, courtyard with fountains and arcades, pilgrims and incense.
Al-Qishla, Baghdad: Ottoman-era brick government building with a tall clock tower, wide arcaded courtyard, a cafe at the foot of the Mutanabbi Street end.

Iraqi covered souk: narrow lanes under corrugated or arched roofs, stalls with hanging textiles, spices in open sacks, copperware, shopkeepers on stools, tea glasses, strong beams of light through gaps.
Masgouf: whole carp split open and propped on stakes around an open wood fire on the riverbank, flames licking the fish, served with sliced onion, tomato and flat bread.
